_disclaimer: Discovery/screening inventory only. A screen_decision here is NOT a clinical determination and does not by itself authorize any patient-visible content -- every item still requires its own evidence and safety review before anything is published. Wikipedia is used exclusively as a taxonomy/discovery aid per its evidence_eligibility=ineligible_tertiary_or_encyclopedia in source_registry.json; no entry's efficacy, safety, mechanism, or cultural-origin claim may be cited to Wikipedia.

source_snapshot.revision_note: Collaboratively edited page; no fixed revision id captured in this pass. Re-snapshot before relying on this inventory again.
source_snapshot.license: Wikipedia article text is CC BY-SA 4.0; this file stores only a modality-name index and screening decisions, not reproduced article text.

methodology: Every modality named on the page falls into one of two buckets below: (1) a documented, auditable group-exclusion rule for non-ingestible categories (energy practices, manipulation/bodywork, divination/spiritual practices, devices, alternative diagnoses, exercise/movement) -- screened out as a group with named representative examples rather than one row per entry, because none of them involve an ingestible botanical, fungus, tea, food, diet, culinary practice, dietary supplement, or plant-derived product; or (2) an individual row in ingestible_candidates or brief_mandated_additions below for anything that DOES involve ingestion. This keeps coverage auditable (every section of the source page maps to a rule) without reproducing an unnecessary ~250-row transcription of the source page.

non_ingestible_group_exclusions.reason: No ingestible component; these are energy-manipulation or belief-based practices with no botanical, food, or supplement involved.

Physical/manual techniques, no ingestible component. Moxibustion and Tui na are procedurally associated with TCM but are explicitly out of scope for this ingestible-herb/nutrition proposal per instruction, even though they share a cultural system with the in-scope material.

representative_entries: Chinese pulse diagnosis (as a diagnostic act)
Chronic Lyme disease (as an alternative diagnosis construct)
non_ingestible_group_exclusions.reason: Diagnostic or device-based constructs, not ingestible interventions. Chinese pulse/tongue diagnosis is explicitly out of scope for this proposal's patient-facing content regardless (this module never provides pattern/syndrome diagnosis).

Movement/mind-body practices, no ingestible component. Tai chi and qigong are culturally associated with Chinese medicine but are explicitly out of scope for this ingestible-herb/nutrition proposal per instruction.

non_ingestible_group_exclusions.group_label: Devices, injections, and procedures not covered by this ingestible-focused module
non_ingestible_group_exclusions.reason: Procedural/device interventions, no plant-derived ingestible product. Registered here rather than silently dropped because some (e.g. chelation, ozone) intersect cancer-quackery risk; a future safety-surveillance module outside this proposal's scope may need them.

ingestible_candidates.modality: Chinese herbology / Chinese herbal medicine / Chinese medicine (herbal branch)
ingestible_candidates.notes: The core subject of this proposal; represented as cancer-context evidence cards, never as a recommendation list.
Traditional dietary-therapy concepts are labeled as cultural/traditional context in diet_template_examples.json, never as biomedical rationale.

ingestible_candidates.modality: Medicinal mushrooms generally (Ganoderma/reishi, Trametes versicolor/turkey-tail/PSK, others)
ingestible_candidates.cultural_system: Overlaps TCM and other East Asian systems; also sold as generic supplements
ingestible_candidates.notes: Modeled with strict species/extract/product non-equivalence -- see card-ganoderma-mixed-cancers and card-psk-resected-gi-cancer in example_evidence_cards.json.
Links to the separate, currently unmerged proposal/ayurveda-oncology-support branch. Not conflated with TCM.
Links to the separate, currently unmerged proposal/homeopathy-oncology-evidence branch. Bach flower remedies are a homeopathy-adjacent system, not TCM, and are not addressed by this module.

Distinct medical system with its own formula tradition (often derived from classical Chinese texts but independently standardized under Japanese regulation). Not relabeled as TCM; no module exists for it in this repository yet.
Distinct system; Korean/Panax ginseng research is noted under the ginseng species-distinction cards but the broader Korean medical system is not addressed here.
Shares some historical formula lineage with TCM but is its own system; not relabeled as TCM.
An eclectic system that may prescribe herbs from many traditions plus supplements, diet, and other modalities; not itself TCM and not addressed as a system by this module.
Distinct herbal tradition from TCM; a Western-herbalism oncology module, if ever built, would be its own separately named proposal.

ingestible_candidates.cultural_system: Originated from a Japanese Zen-influenced dietary philosophy, later Westernized
ingestible_candidates.notes: No qualifying human oncology evidence that a macrobiotic diet treats cancer; strict versions risk nutritional inadequacy during active treatment.

ingestible_candidates.cultural_system: Not a traditional system; modern pseudoscientific framework
ingestible_candidates.notes: The premise that diet meaningfully alters tumor/blood pH to treat cancer is not supported by current evidence.
No qualifying evidence of cancer benefit; potential to displace nutrition/hydration needed during treatment.
Documented harm reports (electrolyte disturbance, infection, bowel injury) and no oncology benefit evidence; explicitly excluded per instruction.
No oncology benefit evidence; argyria and drug-interaction risk.
Associated with reported serious harm (severe electrolyte disturbance); no oncology evidence.
Industrial bleach precursor (chlorine dioxide); documented severe harm; regulatory warnings in multiple jurisdictions; never a food or supplement equivalent.

ingestible_candidates.cultural_system: Traditional practice in some regions, unrelated to TCM
ingestible_candidates.notes: No oncology evidence; documented infectious-disease risk (e.g. MERS-CoV association) independent of any cancer question.

Caustic topical product marketed for skin cancer; documented tissue destruction and disfigurement; not ingestible but flagged given severity and frequent co-marketing alongside ingestible 'natural cancer cure' products.
Documented cardiac, renal, and fatal adverse events; no oncology evidence.
High-dose antioxidant/vitamin supplementation requires oncology-pharmacy review given potential interference with radiotherapy/chemotherapy oxidative mechanisms; never an automatic supplement stack.
A medically indicated fasting or fasting-mimicking protocol requires its own specialist pathway; cannot become generic cancer nutrition content in this module.

Any concentrated supplement form of an otherwise-food ingredient (e.g. curcumin extract, EGCG concentrate) is routed through the same interaction/safety review as a TCM herb extract, never treated as an ordinary food.

brief_mandated_additions_not_individuall.cultural_system: Marketed herbal mixture with a distinct North American origin story; NOT TCM
brief_mandated_additions_not_individuall.notes: Preserved as its own distinct cultural/marketing history per source-assessment.md; NCI and Cancer Research UK report no clear anticancer evidence, and Flor Essence has an animal-model signal for possibly INCREASED tumor formation. Never relabeled as Chinese medicine.

brief_mandated_additions_not_individuall.category: Mistletoe (as injection vs. tea vs. food)
brief_mandated_additions_not_individuall.notes: Injectable mistletoe extract is a distinct, jurisdiction-regulated pharmaceutical product in some countries and is never equivalent to mistletoe tea or treated as an ordinary food; out of scope for this TCM-focused module.

brief_mandated_additions_not_individuall.cultural_system: Not TCM; a regulated pharmacologic topic in most jurisdictions
brief_mandated_additions_not_individuall.notes: Jurisdiction-specific symptom evidence (e.g. nausea, appetite) exists but cannabis is a regulated drug topic, not an ordinary herb or food, and is explicitly out of scope for this ingestible-herb/nutrition proposal.

Cyanide-toxicity risk is well documented; NCI reports no efficacy and real harm potential. This is a toxicity/avoid safety record, never a food recommendation, despite apricot kernels' food-adjacent appearance.

Involves coffee enemas, extreme dietary restriction, and large-volume raw juicing; documented harm potential and no oncology benefit evidence; explicitly excluded per instruction alongside coffee enemas and raw-food/juice regimens.
A medically indicated therapeutic ketogenic diet requires its own specialist nutrition/metabolic pathway; cannot become generic cancer nutrition content in this module.

brief_mandated_additions_not_individuall.cultural_system: Overlaps several wellness movements; not TCM
brief_mandated_additions_not_individuall.notes: Food-safety and malnutrition risk, especially during neutropenia; any juice mention in this module's nutrition templates must be individualized by an oncology dietitian, never presented as anticancer.
Same handling as Orthomolecular medicine/Megavitamin therapy above; potential interference with radiotherapy/chemotherapy mechanisms.
